newsitem.title: CANADA: WCE oilseeds and feed grains end lower.
newsitem.headline: WCE oilseeds and feed grains end lower.

text.p: WCE oilseed and feedgrain markets closed lower, with some selling in all the markets attributed to lower CBOT grain and soy futures, traders said.
Feed grains were lower, pressured by increased hedging of cash purchases and lower CBOT corn futures.

A spate of shortcovering immediately ahead of the close trimmed losses in canola, while the two nearby flaxseed contracts closed at contract lows. The shortcovering was thought to be position squaring ahead of Monday's Statistics Canada Canadian grain stocks report.
Canola closed down $0.60 to $3.60, with March off $0.90 at $405.10 per tonne.
Flaxseed closed down $3.70 to $1.50, with March off $3.00 at $343.20. Hedging of cash purchases was light in oilseeds late.

Feed grains were lower, with commercial buying under the markets. Wheat was off $0.60 to $2.10 with March off $0.60 at $170.00. Barley was off $1.20 to $2.20 with February off $1.20 at $136.50. First delivery day for February barley is Monday.
Oats and feed peas had not traded.
(All values in Canadian dollars except oats and peas.)
(The Canadian dollar rose at midday to $1.3468).
